Body: I have the same issue
No promotions here btw

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #46166: "Instance service init has no timeout and can hang the bootstrap layer indefinitely" — closely related to the no-timeout behavior on bootstrap you describe
- #44684: Plugin installer times out fetching from registry.npmjs.org causing boot hang in headless/serve mode — covers the same plugin dep-install blocking symptom

If either of those covers your case, consider commenting there to add your evidence (pcap data and docker reproduction steps would be valuable additions). If your issue is genuinely distinct, feel free to clarify the differences.

Confirming this still reproduces on **1.18.26 and 1.18.27** (issue was filed against 1.18.21) — same error, same shape, in a Docker sandbox:

```
WARN message="background dependency install failed" dir=/workspace/.opencode
     error="Cause([Fail(NpmInstallFailedError (cause: FetchError: request to https://registry.npmjs.org/@opencode-ai%2fplugin failed, reason: …))])"
WARN (same for dir=/home/analyst/.config/opencode)
```

Extra data points from a week of probing (InsightForge per-project `opencode serve` containers):

1. **The trigger is the plugin file's mere presence, not its imports** — a minimal plugin with zero imports (`export const AskUser = async () => ({ tool: { ask_user: {...} } })`, no `import` statements at all) triggers the same install and the same hang. The installer apparently always wants `@opencode-ai/plugin` from the registry.

2. **Pre-installing the SDK does NOT bypass the installer.** We ship `@opencode-ai/plugin@<same version as opencode>` globally in the image and an entrypoint copies it into `/workspace/.opencode/node_modules/@opencode-ai/` before boot. npm still re-runs its install step and bootstrap still waits for it — the wait is not eliminated by the deps being locally present.

3. **No env switch helps.** `OPENCODE_STRICT_CONFIG_DEPS=false` has no effect in vivo on 1.18.26/1.18.27 (the flag exists per the docs; the boot still waits). `--pure` bypasses the wait (~2s boot) but disables ALL plugins, so it's debugging-only for us.

4. **A second, separate bootstrap wait exists: the models.opencode.ai (models.dev catalog) fetch.** It's *also* in the bootstrap-critical path: on a network where the connection to `172.66.173.149:443` establishes and then goes silent (zero payload — pcap-verified 210s+), the first `POST /session` hangs for minutes. `curl` to the same URL from the same container: 200 in 0.29s. `--add-host models.opencode.ai:127.0.0.1` (fails the fetch <1s, connection-refused) removes that chunk of the stall loss-free — we never use the free catalog. That half is covered by #41360 (fetch failing at boot) + #46166 (no timeout in the bootstrap layer).

5. **Headless impact matches the reporter's**: `GET /global/health` answers instantly the whole time, so any health-check-gated readiness (our backend warms containers on boot) passes while `POST /session` is still blocked — the hang is invisible to health probes.

Mitigations we ship (help, don't fix): `docker run --add-host models.opencode.ai:127.0.0.1`, global SDK pre-install + workspace seed, backend warm-up retry-firing `POST /session`. Net on our worst network: 295s provisioning → ~152s. On clean networks boot-to-session is ~2s.

Full write-up with pcap + probe scripts: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/47279 (same report, filed before triage pointed me here — happy to consolidate).

Adding evidence from a production-ish reproduction (InsightForge per-project `opencode serve` containers, Docker Desktop on macOS, arm64, Ubuntu 22.04 sandbox, opencode 1.18.26 + 1.18.27 — the no-timeout bootstrap hang described here is exactly what we hit):

**Two stacked bootstrap waits observed, both in the critical path of the first `POST /session`:**

1. **models.opencode.ai (models.dev catalog) fetch, no effective timeout.** On our network the TCP connect to `172.66.173.149:443` succeeds and then goes **silent for 210s+** (zero payload bytes; pcap + `/proc/net/tcp` sampled every 3s show ESTABLISHED snapshot 2→70). During the entire hang `GET /global/health` answers instantly while `POST /session` blocks — so the un-bounded init hides behind health checks. `curl` to the same URL from the same container: **200 in 0.29s**, so it's specifically the bootstrap client's fetch pattern (~50 parallel TLS connections) getting hung/throttled.

2. **The plugin "background dependency install" wait** (covered precisely in #44684 — same `NpmInstallFailedError … registry.npmjs.org/@opencode-ai%2fplugin` error on 1.18.26/1.18.27). Notably the trigger is the plugin file's *presence*, not its imports — a zero-import plugin stalls identically; pre-seeding `node_modules` does not bypass the installer; `OPENCODE_STRICT_CONFIG_DEPS=false` has no effect in vivo.

**Measured impact on our worst-case network:** fresh container → first successful session: **295s** before mitigations, **~152s** after (blocking the catalog host via `docker run --add-host models.opencode.ai:127.0.0.1` removes the dominant hang loss-free — we never use the free catalog). With `--pure` (no plugins) boot-to-session is **~2s** — consistent with the plugin path being the residual blocker.

This matches the OP's structural point exactly: `catchCause` only fires on rejection, not hang; and unlike this issue's synthetic never-resolving `init()`, our hang is a *real* service (the npm installer / models fetch) whose Effect lacks a timeout. The two upstream fixes we'd need:

- per-service timeout + warning in `InstanceBootstrap.run` (this issue), and
- making the models.dev fetch + plugin dep-install **non-blocking/async** with fallbacks (#41360, #44684).

Full reproduction + pcap + probe scripts: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/47279 (consolidated report; happy to move everything here if maintainers prefer).

Closing as duplicate after maintainer/triage pointers — this report is the union of two existing issues:

- #46166 — the bootstrap layer has no timeout; any hung service init (here: the models.opencode.ai catalog fetch, zero-payload-ESTABLISHED for 210s+) blocks the first `POST /session` indefinitely. Evidence added there: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/46166#issuecomment-5540221248
- #44684 — the plugin dependency installer hangs headless boot with any .ts plugin (same NpmInstallFailedError on 1.18.26/1.18.27 as originally filed on 1.18.21; zero-import plugins trigger it too; pre-seeded node_modules does not bypass it; OPENCODE_STRICT_CONFIG_DEPS=false has no effect). Evidence added there: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/44684#issuecomment-5540220994

InsightForge-side mitigations that remain valid regardless of upstream fixes: `docker run --add-host models.opencode.ai:127.0.0.1` + global @opencode-ai/plugin pre-install + workspace seed + backend warm-up retry. Full pcap/probe write-up stays at https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/47279 for reference. Thanks for the pointers — following both threads.

**Update:** the primary cause in this report is now avoidable, because AWS changed the endpoint options.

When I opened this issue, GPT-5.6 was available only on the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint. That endpoint uses the OpenAI Responses API, and OpenCode hardcodes `store: false` for it. As a result, every assistant reasoning block is re-sent with its `encrypted_content` on each later turn, and the cost increases with the length of the session.

On **17 August 2026**, AWS made GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna available on the standard `bedrock-runtime` endpoint. That endpoint also supports the Converse API and cross-Region inference profiles, for example `us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol` and `global.openai.gpt-5.6-sol`.

- Launch announcement: https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/08/amazon-bedrock-cross-region-openai-v2/
- Blog post with code examples: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/introducing-cross-region-inference-for-openai-gpt-5-6-models-on-amazon-bedrock/

I confirmed with a live call that the `amazon-bedrock` provider in OpenCode calls `us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol` correctly through the Converse API. This path does not replay the encrypted reasoning blocks, therefore request A is no longer necessary for users who select an inference profile ID.

Request A is still correct for users who must stay on `bedrock-mantle`. AWS keeps that endpoint for workloads with an in-Region requirement, and for server-side tool use.

Request B is not related to the endpoint and is still open. The `truncateToolOutput` helper runs only during compaction, therefore large tool results continue to accumulate on each turn for every provider.

I'd like to take this one. Root cause is in `packages/client/src/solid/connection.ts`: `pagehide` always stops the stream, but `pageshow` only calls `start()` when `event.persisted` is true — returning from background without the bfcache (most mobile and plain tab-return scenarios) leaves the stream dead. `start()` is already idempotent, so `pageshow` can restart unconditionally; bfcache restores, plain tab returns and mobile re-shows all recover. This also covers the same gap reported in #47258. Will include a lifecycle test.
Same root cause as #39030 (the `pageshow` handler only restarts the stream after a bfcache restore) — picking both up in one fix there.

### Description

OpenCode Desktop crashes its local backend (sidecar) a few minutes after **any turn
that actually edits files / does real tool work**, on Windows. After the sidecar dies
the UI can no longer reach it, so every subsequent "Send" fails with
`发送信息失败` / `Failed to fetch` until the app is fully restarted. The app does
**not** auto-restart the sidecar.

This was reproduced **6 times in a single session**, with clean negative controls
(trivial text-only replies, read-only explore turns and long idle periods do **not**
crash). It is not caused by plugins (none installed), not by quota, not by
session/data size, not by memory pressure (sidecar stays ~170–330 MB and never
climbs), and it is **not fixed by `"snapshot": false`**.

The crash signature matches the existing reports in #26667 / #27755 / #45409 —
reproduced here on the **latest** version (1.18.27).

### Plugins

No third-party plugins installed.

### OpenCode version

OpenCode Desktop **1.18.27** (auto-update channel `latest`, says up-to-date).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch OpenCode Desktop on Windows (renderer is served over the `oc://` scheme;
   the engine runs in a Node utility sidecar on `http://127.0.0.1:<random port>`).
2. Open a session and ask the agent to do a real task that **writes/edits files**
   (modify a source file, format several files, or spawn an explore subagent after
   an edit) in a normal code project.
3. Let the turn finish (log shows `exiting loop`).
4. Do nothing for ~2–5 minutes.
5. Send the next message → it fails immediately with `发送信息失败` / `Failed to
   fetch`. Every further send fails too, until you fully close and relaunch the app.

> Note: the crash also occurred once *while* an explore subagent was still streaming
> steps (not only while idle after a finished turn). Trivial Q&A turns ("reply only",
> no tool calls) completed fine and did not crash even after 6+ minutes of idle.

### Screenshot and/or share link

Error toast text: `发送信息失败` followed by `Failed to fetch` (renderer
`TypeError: Failed to fetch`).

### Operating System

Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 (build 10.0.19044). Also reported by others on
Windows 11 (#26667/#27755/#45409).

---

**1. The sidecar crashes with a Windows fail-fast code, then the renderer loses it.**

`<user AppData>\ai.opencode.desktop\logs\<run>\utility.log` (identical on every crash):


`...\logs\<run>\renderer.log` right after the crash, when the user hits Send:
```

```

No `spawning sidecar` line appears again in `main.log` after the crash → the app
does not restart it.

**2. Timing correlation (same machine, same day):**

I may have found a provider-level workaround for both symptoms described here:

https://gist.github.com/mvallebr/877f2dabb5da269091d2e2725a77b218

The configuration routes MiniMax-M3 through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` endpoint and enables `reasoning_split: true`. This makes MiniMax return reasoning separately instead of embedding `<think>...</think>` in `content`. It also avoids the Anthropic-compatible `message_delta` shape where `usage` may be omitted.

I have not yet confirmed this against the exact OpenCode version from this issue, but it may be worth testing.

This looks closely related to a workaround I documented here:

https://gist.github.com/mvallebr/877f2dabb5da269091d2e2725a77b218

MiniMax-M3’s OpenAI-compatible endpoint can return reasoning embedded in `delta.content` unless `reasoning_split: true` is included in the request. With that option enabled, the API returns separate reasoning fields and clean answer content. This may prevent OpenCode from saving a turn containing only a `reasoning` part and no `text` or `tool` part.

The configuration also explicitly sets `thinking.type` to `adaptive`. If this is confirmed, perhaps the same handling could eventually be incorporated into OpenCode’s default MiniMax provider, so users would not need a custom provider configuration.

Verification update, and a note on how general this is.

This isn't a macOS-specific patch — it's about the x86 baseline. Since Bun 1.4.0 the macOS-x64 artifact runs without AVX2, so pinning it puts opencode's CPU floor at Bun's own x86-64 baseline (SSE4.2/POPCNT, x86-64-v2) instead of today's AVX2 (v3). Any pre-Haswell x86 machine gains, and it's the same floor `opencode-linux-x64-baseline` already has — macOS x64 was just the build where Bun 1.3.14's baseline artifact was a byte-identical copy of the AVX2 one, so `--target=bun-darwin-x64-baseline` had nothing baseline to embed.

What I verified on a pre-AVX2 box (Xeon E5-1620 v2 — Ivy Bridge: AVX, no AVX2/FMA/BMI2; macOS 12.7.6), running opencode 1.18.27's own bundle on the Bun 1.4.1 runtime:

- the **TUI renders** — OpenTUI's `libopentui.dylib` loads and paints the UI, not just `--version`
- `opencode serve` answers HTTP on `/config`
- startup ~1.2s

The cause looks like the step-limit prompt being appended as an assistant message, which makes the request end on a model turn.

Both request-building paths do this. `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts:1281` (AI SDK path):

```ts
...(isLastStep ? [{ role: "assistant" as const, content: MAX_STEPS_PROMPT }] : []),
```

and `packages/core/src/session/runner/llm.ts:218` (native path, `:225` on `v2`):

```ts
...(isLastStep ? [Message.assistant(MAX_STEPS_PROMPT)] : [])
```

Assistant prefill works on Anthropic but Gemini has no equivalent and rejects it. Reproduced against `gemini-3.8-flash` with identical history, only the last turn's role differing:

```
contents ending on a model turn -> 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT: Requests ending with a model turn are not supported.
contents ending on a user turn  -> 200
```

That also explains why it mostly shows up on subagents: `steps` has no default, so it only triggers on agents that configure it.

Sending that prompt as a user turn fixes it. I checked the instruction still lands — the model replies with the "maximum steps reached" summary it asks for — and tools are already disabled for that step via `toolChoice: "none"`, so the constraint isn't relying on the message role. It's also consistent with how the runner already injects synthetic input, compaction checkpoints and chronological system updates, which all ride in user turns.

I have this working on both `dev` and `v2` with the suites passing. Happy to open a PR if useful — which branch would you prefer? #40455 looks like the same prefill causing a 400 on Claude 4.6+, so a fix here would likely cover that too.
